exercise.name: Machine Inner Chest Press

reference.title: Machine Inner Chest Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Chest press machine with inner (close, neutral) handles

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come back, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s back, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press with the back on the pad and the shoulders down.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit with the back on the pad and the feet flat; take the inner handles with the palms facing each other, hands about a fist apart in front of the sternum.
Breathe in and let the handles come back to the middle of the chest, elbows close to the sides.
Pause with the hands just in front of the sternum; shoulders down on the pad.
Breathe out and press straight forward, hands staying close, until the arms are long.
Squeeze the inner chest and triceps with the arms long.

mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows close to the trunk; the hands stay close together.
Keep the back on the pad; lighten the stack.
Keep the wrists straight over the handles.

kinematics.norm: From well bent with the hands beside the chest to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
Elbows kept close, about 20-35 degrees from the trunk (clinical opinion)
Neutral: palms facing each other on vertical inner handles, hands close (clinical opinion)
The handles ride the lever arc straight in front of the sternum (clinical opinion)
Back on the pad, little trunk work compared with free-weight or standing presses (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012)
A narrow hand position raised triceps activity in push-ups compared with wide hands (Kim 2016)
Controlled, about 2 s back and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #22801, Machine Inner Chest Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light and press without the back leaving the pad.
At the end of the set let the handles come back under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the hands stop in front of the chest.
Low back discomfort: keep both feet flat and the back on the pad.
progressions: Slower return with a pause at the chest.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover; the close neutral grip keeps the arms in front of the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover; the close neutral grip keeps the arms in front of the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Works hard with the elbows tucked and the hands close (Kim 2016 for narrow hands).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Works hard with the elbows tucked and the hands close (Kim 2016 for narrow hands).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.core: Little demand with the back on the pad (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Controls the elbow on the return.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Controls the elbow on the return.
